newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet votes shareholder protection rules.
newsitem.headline: Eramet votes shareholder protection rules.

text.p: The French state holding company that controls nickel mining firm Eramet approved resolutions protecting minority shareholders presented by U.S. and British funds at the annual meeting on Thursday.
The resolutions, presented by such giants as Fidelity, Mercury and TIAA-CREF, following a fight over what shareholders viewed as management conflicts at the firm.
State-owned Erap owns 55 percent of Eramet.

Last year the conservative government proposed expropriating a mining licence in New Caledonia from Eramet and transfering it to separatist Kanak interests teamed with Canada's Falconbridge in the northern part of the island to quell political tensions.

The resolutions put forward at the AGM included one stating that "the directors' mandate is to defend under all circumstances the interests of the company Eramet and foreswear, in the exercise of their functions, any prejudicial action or inaction".
Another resolution said any exchange of reserves must be justified with regard to the company's interests and those of the island, with internationally recognised experts advising on any decision.
Another resolution required directors to abstain in the event of conflict of interests.
